Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

there! interjection

see? there you are

also see?, there you are, there you go, ta-da, I told you so, didn’t I tell you?

classical

Plaut. Aul. 641: Em tibi, ostendī, eccās.
Plaut. Men. 625b: Em rūrsum nunc nūgās agis.

Em!

there! (showing, or pointing to what has happened)

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Lewis & Short: the same word as ēn, in the best manuscripts of Plautus and Terence (older editions print hem). With tibi, the flourish of “ta-da!”. For handing something over, see here you are.

Other words

  • Vidēn’? — see? do you see?

    clipped vidēsne · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 834: vidēn’ convīvium?; Cic. Att. 13.20.4: vidēn’ quam φιλοσόφως?

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut.; Cic. in epistulīs)

    The vowel keeps the length of vidēs, as the house writes audīn’ from audīs.

  • Dīxīn’? — didn’t I tell you?

    clipped dīxīne, often with tibi · also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 283: Dīxīn’ tibi esse hīc sȳcophantās plūrumōs?

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Examples

  • Ostende hūc manūs. — Em tibi, ostendī, eccās.

    Show me your hands. — There, I’ve shown you: here they are.Plaut. Aul. 640b–641

  • Em rūrsum nunc nūgās agis.

    There, now you’re talking nonsense again.Plaut. Men. 625b

  • sed vidēn’? fortūna hūmāna fingit artatque ut lubet

    but do you see? fortune shapes and squeezes men as she likesPlaut. Capt. 304

  • Dīxīn’ tibi esse hīc sȳcophantās plūrumōs?

    Didn’t I tell you there were plenty of tricksters here?Plaut. Men. 283

See also look!, here you are, I get it!.
